newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to advise Japan on deregulation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to advise Japan on deregulation.

text.p: The United States will advise Japan as it deregulates key sectors of the Japanese economy under an agreement reached early Thursday morning, U.S. officials said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters the agreement would allow U.S. officials to have input in Japan's deregulation though "bilateral consultations" on such areas as telecommunications, financial services and medical equipment.

Officials said the agreement was designed to increase U.S. market access to Japan, which would reduce the two countries' growing trade imbalance, and stressed that it gave Washington only an "advisory role".
"They recognise that the trade imbalance works to their long-term detriment," U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told reporters.
She said this would be the first time that the United States would have such a role in seeking to affect Japanese policy.

Clinton, who arrived in Denver on Thursday for a weekend summit with leaders of the Group of Seven industrialised countries and Russia, told Japan's Fuji television network he was concerned about Tokyo's large trade surplus with the United States, but said he understood Japan was taking steps to boost domestic economic demand.
Earlier on Thursday, the U.S. Commerce Department said that the U.S. deficit with Japan grew by 5.1 percent to $4.84 billion in April.
On Wednesday, Japan said that its merchandise trade surplus with the United States surged 93 percent in May from a year earlier to 322.87 billion yen ($2.85 billion).
Barshefsky described the agreement as "very exciting" and said the potential trade in the sectors involved was "very substantial."
